'''Mark Louis Tomforde''' is an American mathematician who works on [[operator algebra]]s and [[C*-algebra]]s, topics in the broader area of [[functional analysis]].  He held academic positions at the [[University of Houston]] and at the [[University of Colorado Colorado Springs]].

==Biography==
Tomforde earned his Ph.D. in mathematics at [[Dartmouth College]] in 2002.<ref>{{MathGenealogy| 58455}}</ref>

He was an invited speaker at the 2015 Abel Symposium,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abelsymposium.no/2015|title=The Abel Symposium: 2015 symposium|website=abelsymposium.no}}</ref> and he is a founding member of the Algebras and Rings in Colorado Springs (ARCS) center.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arcs-center.org/members.html|title=ARCS — Members|website=arcs-center.org}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Tomforde has researched the related areas of [[graph C*-algebra]]s and [[Leavitt path algebra]]s. With Doug Drinen, he is co-creator of the [[Graph C*-algebra#Desingularization|Drinen–Tomforde desingularization]], often simply called desingularization.<ref>Ch.6 of Graph Algebras, Iain Raeburn, CBMS Regional Conference Series in Mathematics, 103. Published for the Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences, Washington, DC; by the American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2005. vi+113 pp. {{ISBN|0-8218-3660-9}}</ref> With [[Gene Abrams]], Tomforde has formulated the Abrams–Tomforde conjectures, and Abrams and Tomforde have verified certain special cases of the conjectures.<ref>Isomorphism and Morita equivalence of graph algebras, Gene Abrams and Mark Tomforde, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 363 (2011), no. 7, 3733-3767.</ref> Tomforde studied [[ultragraph C*-algebra]]s.<ref>A unified approach to Exel-Laca algebras and C*-algebras associated to graphs, Mark Tomforde, J. Operator Theory 50 (2003), no. 2, 345-368.</ref> Tomforde has also been active in organizing several conferences on graph C*-algebras and their generalizations, with the goal of 
bringing together analysts and algebraists to share ideas and collaborate.<ref>"Graph Algebras: Operator Algebras We Can See", NSF-CBMS Regional Conference in the Mathematical Sciences, Principal Lecturer: Iain Raeburn, Organizers: Paul Muhly, David Pask, and Paul Muhly, University of Iowa, June 2004 {{citation|url=https://marktomforde.com/cv/img/2004CBMS/cbms.html|title=Conference Website|access-date=2020-08-16|archive-date=2022-11-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130074817/https://marktomforde.com/cv/img/2004CBMS/cbms.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>"Graph Algebras in Analysis and Algebra", Special Session at the AMS/MAA Joint Mathematics Meetings, Organizers: Gene Abrams and Mark Tomforde, San Francisco, CA, January 2010 {{citation|url=http://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm/2124_program_ss21.html|title=Special Session Website}}</ref><ref>"Graph Algebras: Bridges between graph C*-algebras and Leavitt path algebras", 5-day workshop at the [[Banff International Research Station (BIRS)]], Main Organizer: Mark Tomforde, April 2013 {{citation|url=http://www.birs.ca/events/2013/5-day-workshops/13w5049|title=Workshop Website}}</ref><ref>"Classification of C*-algebras, Flow Equivalence of Shift Spaces, and Graph and Leavitt Path Algebras", Principal Lecturer: Søren Eilers, Organizers: Gary Birkenmeier, Daniel Davis, P. W. Ng, Leonel Robert, and Mark Tomforde, University of Louisiana at Lafayette, May 2015 {{citation|url=https://userweb.ucs.louisiana.edu/~pwn1677/2015/2015GA.html|title=Conference Website}}</ref><ref>"Workshop on Cuntz-Pimsner Algebras", Organizer: Mark Tomforde, University of Houston, December 2019 {{citation|url=https://marktomforde.com/cv/img/2019Workshop/2019workshop.html|title=Workshop Website|access-date=2020-08-16|archive-date=2022-11-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130074704/https://marktomforde.com/cv/img/2019Workshop/2019workshop.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Tomforde created and directed the [[CHAMP (mathematics outreach program)|Cougars and Houston Area Mathematics Program (CHAMP)]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://champ-outreach.org|title=CHAMP website}}</ref> which was last active in Spring 2019. CHAMP had previously received an award from [[Phi Beta Kappa]]<ref>Phi Beta Kappa Award for Engaging Broader Audiences, {{citation|url=https://champ-outreach.org/images/2018-Spring/PBK.jpg|title=announcement}}</ref>  and the Award for Mathematics Programs that Make a Difference from the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>''[https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201805/rnoti-p552.pdf Mathematics Programs That Make a Difference]''
[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] Vol. 65, Num. 5, May 2018</ref><ref>''[https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201805/rnoti-p572.pdf Building on a Foundation of Grit: Houston's CHAMP Gives Students Tools for Success in STEM (and Life)]'' by Elizabeth Platt Hamblin, 
[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] Vol. 65, Num. 5, May 2018, p.572--577</ref> In 2019 Tomforde was recognized with the MAA Texas Section's Distinguished College and University Teaching of Mathematics Award. In 2020 he was a recipient of a [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]] from the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/news/mathematical-association-of-america-awards-haimo-awards-at-2020-joint-mathematics-meetings|title=Mathematical Association of America Awards Haimo Awards at 2020 Joint Mathematics Meetings {{pipe}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org}}</ref>
